💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

It has been revealed that the release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to quickly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, said on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon.".

Sources indicate that in a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead rapidly.

In a recent development, but then things began moving quickly in a different direction. "I quit guys. I’m sorry," NotRexed, apparently the head of the project, posted last night on X. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

Later, they added, "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve noted before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Shayder, who had previously predicted rapid progress on the Leonida effort following the release of the Xbox executable, took a more direct approach and simply deleted all of their X posts.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This isn't necessarily the end of work to bring GTA 6 (in a probably not-great state) to PC via AI. Other such projects are underway, and there also appears to be an effort to carry on with Leonida: The website remains up, with a latest name attached as owner, and there's at least one Discord server dedicated to it, although it appears a little less focused at this point than the original Leonida server. A new Github repository (NotRexed also deleted that) has been set up: It's "a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project," according to a note on the project, which adds that "development continues here with its full commit history.".

It has been revealed that the advent of AI greatly simplifies and speeds up the work of bringing console games to PC (as long as you're not too picky about the quality), and that makes life tougher for companies that want to keep a lid on such projects. Still, it's not surprising that Take-Two and Rockstar are going hard on it: In the past, Take-Two has moved aggressively to shut down GTA 5 mod projects, an effort that culminated in its acquisition of the biggest and best of them. I've reached out to Take-Two for more information on the takedown and will patch if I receive a reply.

It has been revealed that andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For those of you out there in love with Grand Theft Auto 6's soundtrack, you'll be happy to know that Rockstar Games have revealed an additional 23 tracks as part of the game's deluxe edition album.

Sources indicate that these tracks, available via streaming services, include songs from artists like HEALTH, Denzel Curry, Playboi Carti, and more. You can find the full track list on the official Rockstar Games music website.

According to recent reports, some of these artists played a significant role in the game. Justice, for example, helped compose the game's original soundtrack and several of their tracks appear throughout the game. There are others, too.

According to recent reports, both Sexyy Red and Denzel Curry voice characters in the game's later chapters. Others like Kodack Black and Freddie Gibbs also show up, too - that's not to mention the huge number of musicians who make an appearance in the game's many radio stations. If you listen through those, you'll hear the voices of Keith Richards, Lana Del Ray, The Alchemist and others.

Industry observers note that musical talent also played an additional role in creating the TV advertisements and highlights you can watch in the game. Zack Fox is one example, as is Weird Al Yankovic. Both wrote parts of the game's enticing and absurd significant screen entertainment - which makes sense given the pair's shared comedy background.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

In a recent development, consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a Newly introduced Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

In a recent development, if the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

So we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in Latest York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

According to recent reports, but why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Industry observers note that let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing important happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in New York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

Sources indicate that and finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a substantial turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

Recent findings suggest that in addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of fresh PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog states, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

Microsoft hasn't declared equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

Elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

The arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Final Fantasy VIIFinal Fantasy VII RevelationYoshinori Kitase.

Remaking Final Fantasy VII into a three-part trilogy was always going to be a project fraught with risk. How do you please diehard fans while offering something latest? How do evolving technologies change how you portray a story or character? At South Korean gaming conference G-Star (as reported by 4Gamer), Final Fantasy VII remake producer Yoshinori Kitase gave a lecture discussing the decisions made by the development team while bringing the story to modern audiences.

Kitase opened the talk by tackling one of the biggest points of contention that has followed the trilogy since the first Remake title: Why change elements of a story people have come to know and love? According to Kitase, this question led to a lot of debate while planning the direction for the trilogy. By returning to this story three decades later, they had to contend with the creative intentions of the original developers, and player interpretations of the game and story over the years. While Kitase, having worked on the original, felt he had the right to change elements of the story, he still considered it necessary to balance this with fan expectations. âWhat do we keep, and what do we change?â was his central question.

Recent findings suggest that this, coupled with how much of the original documentation was lostâsomething Kitase blames on the transition from paper to digital material archiving at the studio at that timeâforced the team to make certain judgement calls when defining things like the size of this new Midgar. Kitase noted he wanted to go further in altering the design of Midgarâs central Mako reactor, getting into a heated debate with game director Naoki Hamaguchi before deciding instead simply to embellish upon the original iconic design.

Sources indicate that ultimately, the team refused to make any changes that would counter Final Fantasy VIIâs core story themes. Instead, they wanted to create a game that could make you âcurious about what happens next, even though you already know the ending,â using increased fidelity to expand on how the story was told, while adding upcoming scenes to induce surprise and deepen the emotional impact of even familiar story beats. Using new technology that vastly surpassed the low-poly models of the original, subtle character acting offered a vast step forward from the exaggerated body movements necessary with the older tech.

Kitase talked about the flashback sequence showing how Barret lost his arm. In the original game, the focus of this scene is on Barretâas he tries to save Dyne from falling to his death, he grabs Dyneâs arm to try and pull him to safety, but in this moment heâs shot, losing his arm and his friend in the process. In the remake, the choice was made to take advantage of the improved technology, and instead frame the scene using dialogue and cinematography from the perspective of Dyne, in order to better communicate and emphasize Barretâs pain and guilt.

In a recent development, similarly, Aerithâs death was elaborated upon so that players felt curious to learn more, rather than being consumed by the immediate sense of grief and loss instilled by the original. Kitase recalled the reactions to that scene at the time, saying the loss of Aerith at the end of disc one made some fearful to insert the next disc. This time the team wanted to create senses of disbelief, denial, and intrigue surrounding this now-iconic scene, opening up the story for surprises further down the line.

Industry observers note that the talk also highlighted a new sequence from next yearâs concluding chapter, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, in order to emphasize the teamâs desire to expand on the portrayals of characters and their perspectives within the familiar shell of the original game’s narrative. The sequence showed off a new sidequest in which players could choose to find a runaway chocobo from the perspective of either Red XIII or Cid. If Red takes on the quest, he needs to find vegetables to tempt the chocobo back. Cid will take a more combat-driven approach.

Industry observers note that based on this talk and other comments made by the team in recent months, it seems fans who had hoped for a conclusion that might take risks and stray from the original could end up disappointed. The emphasis is on a desire is to surprise, but not betray, long-time fans. Thus far, these remakes have been an entertaining return to a fan-favorite adventure, and Final Fantasy VII Revelation will aim to round out the trilogy in a way that satisfies as many as possible. Even if Kitase admits he âdoesnât think it is possibleâ to please everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Recent findings suggest that gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy remarked at the time.

According to recent reports, "That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good.".

But like so many other ambitious newly introduced studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it remarked was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain.".

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) claims the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation.".

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.".

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A former teacher in Kentucky was arrested for a second time after she allegedly violated her bond conditions by holding a newborn baby.

Rachel Clement’s bond was revoked on Monday, November 23, after prosecutors learned of the incident. Clement was arrested for a second time after she held the 2-week-old child when she went to a church that is attached to a school on November 13 to drop off birthday party decorations.

Clement previously pleaded guilty to two counts of sexual abuse and one count of evidence tampering in October after she was caught having a sexual relationship with a student at Henderson High School in Henderson, Kentucky, according to The Hendersonian.

As part of her plea deal, Clement, 29, registered as a sex offender, was barred from school premises and was prohibited from having contact with minors except for her biological niece, according to the outlet.

Recent findings suggest that following her second arrest, Clement’s attorney, Jonathan Coomes, argued that his client was at the church at the pastor’s request. He also told the outlet that she had no contact with school-age children and that she left the premises before students arrived.

Coomes went on to argue that the child that Clement held was “not similar in characteristics to the victim in the present case,” noting that her victim was a teenager. It is not at the moment clear if Clement had a relation to the child in question.

In a recent development, clement is facing up to three years in prison on each sexual abuse charge and five years for evidence tampering. She is scheduled to be sentenced on January 4, 2027.

The former teacher was initially arrested in May when she was accused of sending sexually explicit text messages to a student.

Authorities became aware of Clement’s crime when someone reported her inappropriate relationship with the student to high school officials. After the school contacted police, she was immediately removed from the school.

It has been revealed that starting after the scheduled maintenance on December 1st, players will be able to hop between North American and European data centers at will, or pop over to the Oceanian data centers if they so choose. Here’s the breakdown of the fresh server traffic flows:.

Cross-region Travel Available Beginning Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

Details ðâï¸ðï¸ sqex.to/XCFzq.

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-24T12:00:45.707Z.

In a recent development, square Enix’s reasoning is quite simple; peak player times vary across regions so when the servers are slammed in North America, players can choose a European data center to potentially sidestep thousand-player-deep log-in queues and vice versa. ot only is this a great way to get ahead of the impending server traffic jam, but it’s also a neat social feature that eases some of the siloing that happens between servers.

It has been revealed that presently, if you have a cross-continental friendship, you’d have to make an alternate character on the appropriate data center in order to play together. Cross-region travel will let you port your main character over, letting you quest together and, critically, run endgame content like raids without the need to start from scratch on a latest server. That’s huge and players are suitably hyped for it, hoping that the option to data-center-hop remains available permanently.

According to recent reports, square Enix warns that visiting other data centers might increase latency and encourages players to test it out before Evercold releases in February 2027 to get a feel for it. Also, sorry to Oceanian data center players, you still don’t get to go anywhere for now.

In preparation for Evercold, Square Enix is giving away 30 days of free game time to eligible players and has a fresh item for purchase that'll let you skip Dawntrail.

His passing comes days after he performed at Fan Fest Japan 2026.

Hardware requirements and gender-locked rewards aren't getting players excited.

8.0 is shaping up to be the biggest revamp of the MMORPG since A Realm Reborn.

Those looking to jump into Final Fantasy XI can now access the entire base game without time restrictions.

  • That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that at the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” says Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”.

In a recent development, today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” says Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”.

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Sources indicate that held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” indicates Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”.

It has been revealed that it certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”.

In a recent development, bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

Dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

In a recent development, for actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” indicates Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”.

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

“I think it is the ultimate gift to be able to make people happy,” says Brosnan. “My job is being an entertainer—to take the words of great writing and try to transform it into something that is meaningful and memorable.”.

Speaking of entertaining, the week’s announcement that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond was front of mind. “I wish him every joy and every success. He and I made a movie a number of years ago called Remember Me. I played his father. So I was very, very pleased and joyful for his nomination and now his success, and I believe he will be magnificent.”.

Recent findings suggest that and that creative full circle is exactly what the night was advocating. “Our own Luminaries in Residence program reflects our belief that meaningful hospitality creates genuine connection with extraordinary talents with one another, and with arts,” Bob van den Oord, CEO of Langham Hospitality Group, explained as he took the stage. “The Langham isn’t simply a place to stay, but a place to gather, exchange ideas, and indeed celebrate.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

But Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Head to Belville: It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

In the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker, it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Going into this latest season of 60 Minutes, which premiered in September amid the 2026 TV schedule, there was much speculation as to how the show would fare ratings-wise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss has made headlines for multiple reasons since being hired for the job in October 2025, but one specific aspect of the job she continues to receive backlash for is 60 Minutes. This past summer, Weiss and executive producer Nick Bilton cut ties with several high-profile employees and, more recently, the show has seen losses in viewership. Now, some fresh numbers regarding the news magazine show’s 59th season have arrived, and they mark yet another setback for Weiss and her staff.

Going into this latest season of 60 Minutes, which premiered in September amid the 2026 TV schedule, there was much speculation as to how the show would fare ratings-wise. This latest Nielsen data revision from The Wall Street Journal (via The Independent) suggests that the show has indeed been underperforming with its broadcasts. Per the report, the series averaged 8.3 million viewers for the nine episodes that aired between September 9 and November 16. That marks a 16 percent drop from the previous season.

Months ago, Season 59 premiered to 6.5 million viewers on CBS, and that sum differed from the initial report of 7.7 million (which was not finalized at the time). One of the key commonalities between both reports, however, is that the news program has seen losses within the 25-54 demographic. In that demo, 60 has apparently seen a 25 percent decline compared to last season. This demographic is critical, especially when considering on-air advertising.

These ratings mark another less-than-desired situation for CBS News during what’s been a major year of change for 60 Minutes. In May, correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi were fired along with executive producer Tanya Simon and several others. Just recently, Vega said she found it “disturbing” that she still didn’t know the exact reason she was let go. And, shortly after those moves were made, Scott Pelley was also fired from the show after allegedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the series.

Industry observers note that another topic of discussion revolves around the claims of “journalistic interference” at 60. Series alums like Pelley and Vega have alleged that they were encouraged to insert what they considered to be news bias into their reporting. CBS veteran Dan Rather also chastised Weiss and co. for their reporting. The E-I-C has denied that employees’ editorial autonomy has been taken away from journalists at the company.

With the team at 60 Minutes being aware of the chatter that’s surrounded the show as of late, Bari Weiss recently addressed concerns. She recently spoke at a conference organized by The Information, where she noted the show had been doing “tremendously well.” She also emphasized that her main objective for CBS News as a whole was to build a news media organization built on trust. In doing so, she’s made changes to several programs, with the aforementioned show really receiving a makeover.

Bari Weiss Apparently ‘Arrived Like A Conquering Hero’ At CBS News. Why Things Reportedly Changed.

It has been revealed that after parting ways with Pelley and co., Weiss hired several other broadcasters to fill out 60 Minutes’ newly introduced broadcasting team. Ross Douthat, Gianna Toboni, Sebastian Junger, Sir Trevor Phillips and Ariel Levy were ultimately brought on. Those newcomers are now working alongside the show’s three on-camera veterans: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Just recently, Stahl addressed the backlash she faced due to remaining with the show under Weiss’ leadership and said she did so in order for the series as they know it not to “vanish.”.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

There may still be some level of continuity from a talent perspective, but the ratings still stand. As of this writing, neither Bari Weiss nor anyone else from CBS News has addressed this latest viewership enhancement on 60 Minutes. Time will tell how Weiss, Nick Bilton and more might seek to remedy the situation.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

For one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY.

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come swiftly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3.

As you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

This GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr.

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

If you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

Valente, the author of the novel Mass Effect Andromeda: Annihilation Â and a writer on Universe. She held a Reddit AMA talking about her work on the series and revealed some interesting facts about where BioWareâs head was at when it comes to handling Mass Effect 3âs divergent endings.

In a recent development, though we donât know much about how Universe would have handled whether players chose to destroy synthetic life, take control of the Reapers, or achieve Synthesis, leaks suggest that the game would have accounted for all of those possibilities somehow. According to Valente, ensuring that Universeâs handling of the endings âwouldn’t piss everyone offâ was one of BioWareâs massive priorities. Despite years of fairweather fans saying BioWare should âjust make Destroy canon and move on,â that wasnât the route the studio wanted to take.

I don’t think it’s being naughty to say I (and not only me, but I did a lot on it) worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn’t piss everyone off, at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn’t make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn’t privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel.

Sources indicate that not for nothing, guys, but that’s kind of a tall fucking order. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be really hard. An elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn’t take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible…it takes a long time, and it’s not obvious how best to pull it off when you’re the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing.

And it’s become really clear that it’s impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices. We burned out so many valuable neurons going up against that problem. I know so many people think it’s easy, just make Destroy canon and move on, but consider that, for example, I feel as strongly about Synthesis as others do about Destroy. And everyone feels strongly about choices mattering. Do you really think there is a single solution that would have satisfied everyone? In a video game?

Industry observers note that but we did our best, and I think we landed in a good place. There wasn’t one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can’t say any more than that.

I remember laughing ruefully once and thinking god, if I’d known when I finished ME3 that I’d be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess….

But as I’m saying a lot: yes, there was an answer, yes, I know it, as least inasmuch as I know what it was when I was working there, because part of it was my job, and we tried our damnedest to do right by the story and the fandom. That room was full of ambition and enthusiasm, and I don’t think it could have been in better hands. We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it.

And I asked myself that at the end of everything I did: If I could go back to being just a fan, would I be happy with this?

Often it feels rooted in a desire for more of a thing one likes at any cost, rather than in maintaining the integrity of the seriesâ role-playing and fiction, and usually in these situations, developers arenât looking for an easy way out. BioWare certainly wasnât, at least. Even during pre-release interviews for Dragon Age: The Veilguard, the studio was pretty adamant that it would rather not reference previous game choices than undermine them, though that would be impossible in a Mass Effect game set in the Milky Way after Mass Effect 3, given the galaxy-wide ramifications of the choices you make in that game.

Whatever Universeâs ambitions might have been for acknowledging all of Mass Effect 3âs endings, Valente also emphasized that the game wasnât done and that even the solutions the team was considering at this stage of development might not have been the ones used in the final game if it hadnât been canceled in favor of Star Wars Battlefront III.

âYou have to remember the game wasn’t done,â she wrote. âThings changed all the time, even week to week, and who knows where and how the things I worked on or saw others work on would have ended up in the final game. It’s forever frozen where it was when EA pulled its Renegade Interrupt, but that doesn’t mean that’s what it would have been without it.â.

In a recent development, prince William and Kate Middleton’s visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony marked their first joint overseas tour in four years, and the couple used it as an opportunity to demonstrate their star power. Through their action-packed itinerary, which took them from Mumbai to Newly introduced Delhi, the Prince and Princess of Wales have paved the way for a new style of royal tour.

From Kate unexpectedly presenting an award and delivering a speech at the star-studded Earthshot Prize event to her and William playing cricket and traveling around Mumbai in an electric rickshaw, there have been plenty of photo opportunities and headlines around the world about the environmental initiative William is so passionate about.

Sources indicate that according to royals author Russell Myers, who followed the couple on tour, the speech Kate gave at the awards was kept top secret. “None of us knew she was presenting an award on the night, or that she was going to speak. The auditorium was packed. There were about 5,000 people there. It’s been the biggest Earthshot yet, and you could see Catherine was nervous, but she delivered an absolutely brilliant speech. I’d say her best yet.

“It’s been wonderful for her to be here, supporting William, and you can see they’ve really had fun. Because of ongoing terror threats, there have been less walkabouts, but it’s been a very successful and varied tour, and I think, being shorter than most tours, it sets a new blueprint when it comes to royal tours for the couple in the future.”.

Prince William and Princess Kate arrive to attend the Earthshot Prize awards night at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

There are seemingly already plans for another royal tour, claims Myers.

Industry observers note that “William let slip that Australia is on the cards next, and if that’s the case, I imagine they will go as a family. They don’t want to be away from their children for too long, and what a way it would be to win support for the monarchy Down Under,” Myers notes.

In a recent development, according to royals insiders, there had been some nervousness around the trip after the couple’s disastrous tour of the Caribbean in March 2022, when their visit was overshadowed by calls for the UK to apologize for slavery. Then some of their photo calls, including one that involved the couple riding in an open-top Land Rover, led to accusations of the royals appearing colonial and out of touch.

According to recent reports, “I think there has been a slight nervousness about how this tour would be received, but the reception has been really good,” Myers notes. “The fact that William and Catherine have included a visit to Latest Delhi to see Prime Minister Modi is a clever move. While this is a private trip to promote Earthshot, the Foreign Office was keen for William to meet with the Indian prime minister, so they have packed that into the itinerary too.”.

Recent findings suggest that the visit to India has come at a time when the royals are on something of a charm offensive following a difficult year for the royal family, from Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor’s arrest to what one palace insider calls “the ongoing soap opera” with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has not been charged and has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.).

Sources indicate that william and Kate are keen to carve out their own initiatives and projects focusing on their major priorities, including the environment, children’s early years, and mental health. With the challenge of having Harry and Meghan carrying out their own engagements, the Prince and Princess of Wales have been careful to establish clear parameters that set them apart as working royals. In one telling moment while on an engagement in Mumbai, Kate was asked for an autograph. She politely declined, so as not to breach protocol, a clear contrast to the Duchess of Sussex, who has signed autographs in the past.

In a recent development, “Catherine was asked to sign an autograph, but she was right not to. It wasn’t a snub; it was just adhering to protocol. An autograph could be sold for money,” notes Dickie Arbiter, former press secretary to Queen Elizabeth II.

According to author Tom Bower, the royals are more relatable now than they were during the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, who famously never gave a press interview. In recent weeks, Prince William has appeared as a guest on The Graham Norton Show (to promote Earthshot), and he’s revealed how he drinks his cider and his love of wild swimming as part of his guest-editing stint for a recent issue of Country Life magazine.

Industry observers note that “The royals are more relatable, perhaps, than they ever have been, but they are not celebrities. There’s a danger of being too relatable, too much ‘one of the people,’ which means they can lose some of their mystery,” Bower says.

It has been revealed that “William will have been advised to do TV appearances and take on media opportunities to bolster his public image. Of course, it’s charming to hear these nuggets and see this side of the prince, but I do think there’s a need to see and hear more from William about his broader aims. Over the years, Charles has made huge efforts to appeal to all cultural aspects of society. I’m not sure William has done that. He’s got to find a way of connecting with everyone, not just the younger generation,” Bower adds.

The Earthshot Prize awards have been a powerful way of demonstrating that William doesn’t just talk the talk; he is insisting on action.

“The Earthshot is a master class in what needs to be done,” concludes Arbiter. “He’s pushing for environmental issues and climate change, and he’s getting people to do something about it. The fact that he is so well supported, and by so many high-profile people, indicates his pulling power and influence.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christina Applegate is clapping back at trolls who criticized her for being disappointed that she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t want to sit here and be like, ‘Boo-hoo-hoo me’ all the time about this whole thing because now it’s about kind of getting boots on the ground now and getting myself together,” Applegate, 54, stated during the Tuesday, November 24, episode of her and Jamie Lynn Sigler’s “MeSsy” podcast. “It really does feel good to feel understood because it’s a hard thing to come out and say that I’m upset that I don’t have MS, right?”.

Addressing her critics, the Dead to Me alum continued, “A lot of people had a lot to f***ing say about it after I came out. But, you know, it’s not about that. It’s about an identity thing. … It’s about a community that I love still, as we know.”.

Applegate also pointed out that having a diagnosis allowed her to “relax” into her illness rather than constantly searching for answers about what’s wrong with her health.

“It can be incredibly stressful,” she added.

Applegate first unveiled her battle with what she believed to be MS in 2021. After five years of detailing her health journey and advocating for MS patients, the actress revealed in October that she had been misdiagnosed with the autoimmune disorder.

It has been revealed that “[My doctor] came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’” she said on her podcast at the time. “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”.

Industry observers note that applegate became emotional as she explained, “You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden I’m better. I haven’t gotten better, Jamie! If anything, I’ve gotten worse. So I’m back at square one where I don’t know what’s going on with me. And that’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?”.

The Married… With Children alum added that she went through a “great depression” after the health revelation.

In a recent development, “I lost everything. I lost my job. I lost — I’m sorry. What do you say to someone who’s been living with this for six years — God, I’m so sorry — because it stopped my life,” she said through tears. “I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor’s office. I can’t walk from the car to the room. I’m still in this. Nothing magical happened when she said, ‘You don’t have MS.’ Nothing magical happened.”.

Applegate later shared a theory about what may have caused her MS-like symptoms.

“I had my double mastectomy in 2008, and I am way overdue for having them replaced,” she stated during the November 10 episode of her podcast. (Applegate underwent a double mastectomy after her August 2008 breast cancer diagnosis, followed by breast reconstruction surgery using saline expanders and implants.).

“I swear over the last five years or whatever, I’ve thought, ‘What if they’re leaking and poisoning me?’ And then there was some study … about it presenting as MS,” she continued. “So that’s one that I will be looking into because it’s something I’ve thought about.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a fresh report, the organization is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series.

Industry observers note that the information comes from a new report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone.

Rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the organization is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why.

It's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of shows based on popular video games, such as Fallout. HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers.

Indeed, many more video game-based shows are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series, its God of War adaptation, as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show. Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028.

Industry observers note that but none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods. They're all special custom builds of stock guns and weapons with unique skins, but some of them are way more worth the trouble to hunt down than others. You'll find some of them easily—every Ammu-Nation has a unique gun sitting out for you to buy. The best unique weapons are a little more hidden. There are treasure hunts and easter eggs and a whole lot that you'll grab by fighting your way through a gang hideout.

The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.

Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38.

This is the easiest unique weapon to grab right at the start of the game and totally worth the boat ride to grab it. There isn't even any combat to get to it, like many of these other uniques. The Assassin Nipper comes with a suppressor attachment, which is a really expensive mod to buy early in the game. Pick it up as soon as you've got free range in Key Lento from an old shipwreck in the Permit Keys near the military base location.

It has been revealed that another great Chapter 1 snag is this sniper rifle at a Kingfisher hideout. The combat to get it is minimal (don't get between that tiger and its prey) so it's easy to pick up early. It's a bolt action that can't equip a silencer, so it isn't exactly a stealth tool, but it can help Jason pick off gangsters in a hideout before even going inside. It comes with a stock and a basic dot sight.

It has been revealed that A variant of the Vom Feur V5FC, found in Port Gellhorn at a Kolt gang hideout. It's up on the top floor of the motel by the La Cascara Motel safe, so you pretty much have to complete this illegal operation to grab it. I recommend coming up the south stairwell that's less guarded and hugging the outer walkways to get most of the way to the loot room by stealth. It's worth it though. The Scrapper is a silenced longarm SMG fairly early in the game with an extended mag and a flashy paint job.

This Duke Carbine variant doesn't have a suppressor but it is quite high accuracy for a full auto assault rifle with a heavy stock and 7" pistol barrel mod. The Kolt 556 is easier to smash and grab than the Scrapper, though. You've got to fight in and out of the Kolt stash house, but it's a small joint so it's not too hard to get away clean. It's in a gun case on a kitchen table near the safe full of pills.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • After infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers.
  • The largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

After infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

The largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

"I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Sources indicate that before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but quickly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

According to recent reports, incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

According to recent reports, rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the company has not revealed GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

If you're among the millions already playing the game on consoles, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough contains a wealth of information covering all major mechanics, main missions, secrets, cheats and more besides.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Vermont woman will serve prison time for defrauding an elderly woman she befriended and manipulated in a scheme to steal thousands of dollars from her, federal prosecutors noted.

Industry observers note that chief U.S. District Judge Christina Reiss sentenced Jessica Russell, of Williamstown, to one year and eight months in prison on Friday, November 20, after she pleaded guilty to two federal counts of wire fraud, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont said in a news release.

The judge also ordered Russell, 43, to pay nearly $85,000 in restitution to the victim’s family and imposed a $75,945.16 forfeiture money judgment, according to prosecutors.

The restitution figure, $84,420.16, reflects the amount of money Russell stole from the woman to buy herself a home and a car, prosecutors wrote in a sentencing memorandum obtained by Us.

Sources indicate that russell’s federal public defender, Sara M. Puls, didn’t immediately return a request for comment from Us.

In a recent development, authorities discovered Russell financially took advantage of the woman, who has dementia, after firefighters found the woman “confused and injured, trapped in a filthy residence in Barton, Vermont” during extensive flooding in 2023, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said in its release.

Russell later admitted as part of her plea agreement that she befriended the woman between the summer of 2013 and July 2023, partly by pretending her child had died, as the woman had experienced the death of her own child, according to prosecutors.

She allegedly lied to the woman to endear herself to her, so that the woman “would believe they were both grieving mothers,” prosecutors wrote in the government’s sentencing memorandum.

Russell eventually moved in with the woman and started calling her “mom” as part of her ongoing scheme to manipulate and defraud her, according to prosecutors.

Industry observers note that “As their false friendship grew, Victim 1 executed legal documents giving Russell power to act on Victim 1’s behalf,” the government’s sentencing memo states. “As Victim 1’s dementia advanced, Victim 1 and Russell jointly opened a bank account in Vermont.”.

The woman went on to sell a home she owned in North Carolina and deposited money from the sale into the account she shared with Russell, according to prosecutors. Afterward, Russell allegedly took the money to buy a vehicle and home in Barton, Vermont.

During Russell’s sentencing hearing, the woman’s family members remarked Russell isolated the woman from her sisters, resulting in their unsuccessful attempts to maintain contact with her, prosecutors said.

The government accused Russell of similarly manipulating a second Vermont woman, whose child had died, by posing as a grieving mother and trying to build a friendship with her. Though she didn’t steal from this woman, prosecutors argued the alleged manipulation “shows the depths of her depravity.”.

In a recent development, in a statement, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt said, “it is hard to imagine a more depraved and harmful fraud.”.

“Jessica Russell preyed on the kindness of another, pretending to share grief and manipulating sympathy for her personal, financial gain,” Ophardt continued. “Russell’s multi-year pattern of deception devastated her victims and their families.”.

Cheeky Malware Linked To Popular Gacha Game Cracks City Security

💡 Key Takeaways
  • East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.
  • East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.
  • It has been revealed that one recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses. Gaming has been one of many areas targeted: between arcade games on Sega's network going offline, 11 million Capcom IDs being compromised, and a high-schooler hacking Bandai-Namco, some major publishers have been suffering a string of embarrassments. One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident. Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC. The subcontractor in question, IT services company GIS Hokkaido, would then confirm to Japanese tech news site ITMedia that, yes, NIKKE's compromised PC launcher was the source of the problem. When asked if an employee or subcontractor had launched the game on a work PC, GIS politely replied that "they would prefer not to comment." Moral of the story? While there's nothing wrong with playing a suggestive gacha game on your own time, you probably shouldn't do it on the clock, and definitely not on a company PC, lest you become internet meme fodder.

#188856. Latest Update: This Emerging Artist Is a Hit Restaurateur

Latest Update: This Emerging Artist Is a Hit Restaurateur

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2179 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before.
  • On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades.
  • Industry observers note that the twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Borgo sits on one of those blocks in the high 20s that you swear you’ve never been down before. The restaurant opened in 2024 but feels like it’s been there forever, a place with a natural hum and not an ounce of perspiration. Its clientele is specific but unpredictable; when I went there this summer for lunch with a movie producer, we spotted a powerful name-brand media executive, an architectural bigwig who designs the homes of billionaires, and a two-time Academy Award–winning actor. A few nights later, I sat near Walter Isaacson, who’s a regular. And don’t just take it from Elon Musk’s biographer. Matthew Schneier, the chief restaurant critic at New York magazine, recently named Borgo the city’s best all-around restaurant.

On one occasion, my server was a painter who used to bartend at The Odeon, as painters have done for decades. He met Ross Bleckner there, and David Salle. He used to have a massive loft studio in Williamsburg, but as rents went up, he moved deeper into Brooklyn, to Fort Greene, where he built a studio in his basement.

Industry observers note that the twist is that my server’s art was also hanging on the walls of Borgo, as was his daughter’s art. That’s because he was Andrew Tarlow—the painter and restaurateur who kick-started the Brooklyn aesthetic with his restaurant Diner and, yes, also owns Borgo.

After launching that instant hit in an old, reclaimed diner, Tarlow opened five more era-defining Brooklyn spots before finally venturing into Manhattan with Borgo. All along, he’s still been the artist who got a job at The Odeon so that he could meet his heroes. He’s still painting away in his brownstone, doodling on notepads during concept meetings. He’s had highlights recently at galleries such as Tiwa Select; he’s loosely associated with the Galerie Sardine extended universe; and he’s someone whose work I’ve been told about for years by those in the know.

As they put it, Tarlow is an emerging artist who happens to own the best all-around restaurant in Manhattan, as well as a bunch of other successful spots in Brooklyn.

In a recent development, “I realized, opening Borgo, that I really loved working in restaurants—and not that I had forgotten, but I hadn’t actually worked services in a while until I opened,” Tarlow told me during a studio visit. “And then, in a similar way, I think—I love making paintings. I actually will paint forever, no matter what happens.”.

According to recent reports, the studio had dozens of unstretched canvases heaped on the ground, some still rolled up, and others hanging via a pin on the studio wall. They revealed figures grappling with pain in fierce color-blocked fields, automatic-painting abstractions, faces fading into other faces. One painting was a portrait of the artist Joe Bradley, a friend.

The studio is in the basement of the Fort Greene brownstone where Tarlow has lived for two decades with his wife, Kate Huling, raising four kids in a kind of neo-boho paradise. There were no studio assistants, no art handlers, no frames, no boxes, no packaging—just the artist and the work.

According to recent reports, “It was kind of just as chaotic as everything else there, but in the most perfect warm embrace of a way. I saw the pure energy that he put into his paintings and the stories that they told,” says Alex Tieghi-Walker, the founder of Tiwa Select, calling from London. “So many artists could be quite—rightfully so, but quite precious with their works. And I love that Andrew was just like, ‘Oh, pull out the ones you’re taking and just take them in an Uber home.’”.

Tarlow grabbed at a canvas bare-handed, one with a bit of a conceptual bent, and put it up on an easel.

“I’ve had this up on the wall for a while now, and I just continued to look at it because I’m happy with it. I’m also a little unsettled—I mean, I’m showing you the inside of my drawers. I’m also a little unsettled by how far it’s gone abstract-wise.”.

In a recent development, he told me he couldn’t really do his other job, the restaurant job, without painting at odd hours. They’re totally separate, but complementary in a cosmic way.

“What are the processes? Like you noted, for some people, it’s nine to five. Then you listen to the news, smoke a cigarette, drink coffee. It’s either working or it’s not. The door either opens or it’s not,” Tarlow said, gesturing around to his studio. “But I’m going to go here every day, and I’m going to push some paint on canvas.”.

It has been revealed that diner opened in 1999, a few years after Tarlow moved to the desolate southern tip of Broadway in Williamsburg—where the crumbling street dead-ends into the East River. While looking for a cheap studio space, he found a 6,000-square-foot loft across the street from an abandoned diner from the 1920s. The loft’s landlord bought the diner, and in 1999, Tarlow opened Diner with then partner Mark Firth—and watched as it was patronized by only the artists across the street.

“You could stand outside the restaurant in those days and not see a single person walk by,” he told Bon Appetit in 2010.

It has been revealed that tarlow kept expanding. He opened Marlow & Sons, and then the butcher shop and specialty food store Marlow & Daughters. He founded a bakery, She Wolf, and a literary magazine, Diner Journal. He operated the restaurant at the Wythe Hotel, but only for a few years. Instead of doing the easy thing, Vegas-ifying Diner in some new development on the Williamsburg waterfront, he got even weirder, opening a nautical bar called Achilles Heel in a far-out corner of Greenpoint.

A dealer with a gallery in Tribeca was the first, but far from the last, to tell me I had to check out Tarlow’s paintings. After an introduction was brokered, Tarlow invited me to lunch at Borgo this past summer. The restaurant has many fantastic pork-laden dishes, but we ate almost entirely vegetables, as well as one very elegant, simple piece of fish. A summer lunch. We fell into an easy patter, talking about exhibitions, other artists—but mostly his painting practice. He’d been working on Long Island, not on the East End but in the middle. He’d had a few shows. There was discussion of representation. He spoke about all this with an unpracticed earnestness and complete confidence. He sounded like a very prominent emerging artist, which, at 56, he is.

Sources indicate that “I don’t know if it’s just age or time, or I was too much of a young person, or a young mind, but I’ve been more secure with my ability to hold all these things in the same time,” he told me back in the studio. “I can go work tonight in the restaurant and feel perfectly confident in that work, and I can show you this work and feel perfectly confident in this work. Whereas, I think, as a young person, I felt like, Am I fake?”.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes it’s not the enfant terrible who breaks out—it’s the working parent, the person with a desk job, the successful entrepreneur who back-ends into revolutionary art making. Think William Carlos Williams writing “The Red Wheelbarrow” while working as a doctor in Rutherford, Latest Jersey. Or Ruth Asawa making art in her kitchen while raising six children in San Francisco. Or Jeff Koons working on Wall Street in order to earn money to make his sculptures. Having a demanding job actually granted them the freedom to be artists. Tarlow started drawing during restaurant concept meetings.

Sometimes Tarlow hangs his own paintings upstairs in his brownstone’s salon room, or at his house on Long Island, to see what they look like in the wild. The paintings have a confident thrust to them, with the colors bold-blocked in a way that reminds me of Albert Oehlen, drawing from Roman and Greek mythology in Twombly-esque riffs: visages multiplying and fading like a Kippenberger-ian pomo ride into the ether. Sure, any painter who’s spent time in Europe since the 1990s has wanted to be Martin Kippenberger. But Tarlow has an actual connection to him: Like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a lover of Italian food and good wine, and he made art to hang in restaurants. And like Tarlow, Kippenberger was a restaurant owner, balancing his studio practice with running Capri, a Venice, California, spot in which he invested after moving to Los Angeles in 1989. According to those present at the time, Kippenberger became a part-owner of the place because, as the artist put it, “You can’t get a decent Bolognese in Los Angeles.”.

As a bartender at The Odeon, Tarlow maintained a working painting studio but found it hard to produce art. After opening Diner, he skipped painting sessions in favor of opening businesses and starting a family. Once that duality settled, he started drawing on the move, carrying sketchbooks and working through potential paintings. Eventually, once the kids got old enough, he built out a studio in a nook of his 19th-century basement.

In a recent development, “I really started painting back downstairs. Let’s just say, after dinner, it was 8 p.m. and they were watching Nemo. No one actually needs me, they’re totally happy. My wife’s up there, everyone’s laughing, giggling with little fish,” he said. “And I can just walk down here and do my thing. Having it in my house for sure is the only way I could do this amount of work, and for sure even get to this place. Because I do think you have to do a certain amount of work to get to this place unless you’re just a born prodigy. But when you think about the genius of Picasso or whomever, he made a million fucking paintings.”.

Tarlow didn’t really show anyone his work for a long time.

“I met Andrew socially. I knew his restaurants way before I knew Andrew. And one day he was like, ‘Come and see my studio,’” Tieghi-Walker tells me. “It did not surprise me at all that he had an art studio in his basement and that these were the types of works he was creating.”.

The show at Tiwa Select was on view right as Tarlow was getting ready to open Borgo. There was a certain amount of unconscious transference, Tarlow told me. For the Tiwa dinner, instead of creating name placards, the artist hand-sketched an artwork of each guest’s name on the paper tablecloth. Now, when a regular makes a reservation at Borgo, Tarlow will elegantly sketch out their name on the paper tablecloth.

The showcasing of his art at Borgo marks the first time Tarlow has put his own work on the premises of his own restaurant. Tarlow doesn’t exactly promote this. When I asked about it, he told me that only one of his own works was up at the moment, then changed the subject. Alex Levy, the media strategist and theater producer, has been a regular at Borgo since it opened. “Borgo is the grown-up Platonic ideal of what a restaurant can be,” he said. After several visits, Levy, who also collects a bit of contemporary art, noticed what was on the walls.

It has been revealed that “I complimented one of the paintings, and Andrew said, ‘It’s by my daughter.’ And then he pointed to another one and said, ‘That’s by me,’” Levy says. “I had no idea that there’s this whole other part of him.”.

Like Tarlow, Levy balances two seemingly divergent but strangely complementary careers—as a speechwriter on one hand, a Tony Award winner on the other—and Tarlow invited him to see his studio on Long Island. Levy bought a painting immediately. Seeing the studio, Levy claims, helped him realize, to some extent, what the special sauce is behind a place like Borgo. It’s for incredibly confident, hyperproductive creative types, run by an artist who has complete faith in his ability to work.

And for Tarlow, the focus and passion in one arena lead right into the passion for the other.

“I’m also being very present for your needs in the same way as I’m trying to be very present with these paintings,” he said. “They’re not separate boats. When the restaurant’s working, I feel creative inside of it.”.
