Deborah Nevins—a Legend of Landscape Architecture—Plants With Purpose

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When my partner and I were starting a family, we searched high and low for a place outside New York where we could imagine our future children growing up.
  • It looked like something out of a medieval fairy tale.
  • Industry observers note that our twins’ arrival was imminent, so we made an offer in February, closed in April, and brought home babies Grace and Noah on Memorial Day weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When my partner and I were starting a family, we searched high and low for a place outside New York where we could imagine our future children growing up. We looked upstate, in Connecticut, and at all those charming hamlets strung along the eastern end of Long Island known as the Hamptons. Toured hundreds of houses, clicked thousands of listings. But not one felt like home.

Nevins in her garden in East Hampton.

It looked like something out of a medieval fairy tale. A great furrowed trunk rising from a froth of flowering vines that split into enormous limbs sweeping improbably far across the garden. Its arrangement was so baroque—veiny, muscular wood twisting and reaching, dissolving overhead into a canopy of green delicacy. We could picture our children climbing its winding branches, little hands against its ridged, mossy bark.

Industry observers note that our twins’ arrival was imminent, so we made an offer in February, closed in April, and brought home babies Grace and Noah on Memorial Day weekend. Now we joke that we didn’t buy a house—we bought this tree.

But what is it? A butternut tree? An oak? A black walnut? Deborah Nevins, one of the most revered living landscape designers, created this garden for the previous owners in 2004. In the fall, she invited me to her white-shingled cottage in Springs, East Hampton, to find out. Her living room has triple-hung windows like those in Monticello, Thomas Jefferson’s house in Virginia, which go down to the floor so it’s easy to wheel in her potted lemon trees when the seasons change. “Winter is divine; it’s when they bloom,” she coos. “The house smells of lemon blossoms.”.

David Geffen’s pool at his former Beverly Hills estate, once home to Warner Bros.’ Jack Warner.

It has been revealed that “Butternut!” she declares, slamming the book shut with all the force of her petite five-foot-nothing frame. “For sure.”.

This is our tree. A butternut that likely sprouted generations before she came along. “It’s a native tree, probably a hundred years old. But I’d have to know the caliper—the diameter about a foot up—to be more precise.” She decided it’d be the anchor for our yard design the moment she saw it—existing mature trees are “sacred” and must be preserved at all costs. At its base, she dared to plant clematis, usually a climbing vine, that now rambles across the ground, softening the old tree’s trunk with a tangle of flowers. The butternut divides the rest of the property into distinct passages, including an ornamental reflecting pool bordered by hornbeam hedges, a lap pool shaded under locust trees, and a gravel path lined with rounded boxwoods.

In a recent development, GREEK MYTHOLOGY It took Nevins eight years and some 20 trips to Greece to complete her collaboration with architect Renzo Piano on the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center. What was once a parking lot is now planted with more than 1,500 trees, 128,000 shrubs and perennials, and 164,000 grass plugs.

A rendering of the 40-acre park at the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center in Athens.

Sources indicate that to Nevins, the tree is an excellent example of her greater gardening philosophy: “I’m interested in creating unfolding spaces which intensify [the viewers’] experience, your sense of place and movement through a garden,” she states. She frequently builds hedges and allées to control viewers’ attention, like horse blinders. “Not every aspect of the garden is seen at once. You have to stop and think.”.

Industry observers note that over the last four decades, Nevins has been entrusted with the grounds of some extraordinary spaces. Her clients include media mogul David Geffen, fashion designer Tommy Hilfiger, former Disney chairman Michael Eisner, and hotelier Ian Schrager. Commissions can range from tiny residential spaces (like mine) to huge commercial projects abroad. It took her eight years and some 20 trips to Greece to complete a 40-acre park at the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center in Athens. That was a collaboration with architect Renzo Piano on a landscape that climbs over the buildings themselves, planted with native grasses from the hills of Attica and fragrant Mediterranean herbs, including lavender, rosemary, and oregano. Nevins’s mantra for the project was simple: “Speak Greek.” The execution was anything but simple. More than 1,500 trees, 128,000 shrubs and perennials, and 164,000 grass plugs fill the public work. Nevins conceptualized the totality of the park. “I chose every single tree!” she notes. “We had to propagate hundreds of thousands of plants throughout Greece, and we decided to hire various nurseries so that if there was a disease or fire, the entire crop would not be wiped out.” Her effort impressed Piano. “It is always special when, beyond the work on a project itself, you realize that you share the same values and ideas,” says Piano of Nevins, whom he describes as a “wonderful professional and human adventure.”.

“There is discipline in her work but never rigidity,” says Scott Mitchell, the West Coast–based architect who met Nevins at a dinner honoring architect Richard Meier in 1997 and went on to work with her on properties for Geffen in both California and Newly introduced York. “Her landscapes don’t compete with architecture; they give it a place to belong.”.

He recalls the “emotional power” of her work for Geffen at the Warner estate in Beverly Hills, former home of Warner Bros. cofounder Jack Warner. “Endless sweeps of white azaleas, a driveway lined with ancient, gnarled native sycamores, and 11 acres of rolling meadow beneath giant coast live oaks,” Mitchell says. “World-class projects require cohesion between architecture and landscape. They have to play from the same sheet of music. Debby totally gets that. Her response to architecture is clear and harmonious—confident but never overstepping.”.

Tommy Hilfiger and Dee Ocleppo at their Mustique estate.

Recent findings suggest that gil Schafer, a Latest York–based architect who has worked with Nevins on more than 25 houses and gardens, also commends her command of structure. At his own house near Millbrook, she built a 12-foot-high hornbeam enclosure nestled into the surrounding farm fields that has, he says, “an almost abstract sculptural quality—as if Richard Serra had suddenly decided to work in hornbeam rather than Corten steel.”.

In a recent development, nevins was born in Manhattan at what was then the Doctors Hospital on the Upper East Side. The family resided in the penthouse of the same building where Greta Garbo lived. Her father died of a brain tumor at 43, when Nevins was six months old, and so her mother had to return to work. At six, she was sent to Camp Taconic in Massachusetts. “I was tiny! My mother might have been arrested today.” She remembers walking in the woods, finding a strawberry, and reporting the discovery in a letter home. The seed had been planted—pun quite obvious.

Fleur Cowles, the formidable editor behind the short-lived, extravagantly inventive magazine Flair, was a maternal relative and had an outsize impact on her childhood. “She knew everyone, and she was so brilliant,” Nevins says, offering me an issue of Flair from another bookshelf like a cherished family heirloom. Another influence was her mother’s sister, Miriam Sampson, an interior decorator who lived across from Carnegie Hall. “In this massive apartment, she had her office in one room, and she had little models of apartments. I was so intrigued,” Nevins recalls. She’d cut out pictures of interiors and gardens from magazines and assemble them in scrapbooks. “But I didn’t even know about this idea of being a landscape architect.”.

When Nevins was 14, her mother remarried and the family moved to New Haven, Connecticut. She went on to attend Boston University for undergrad and returned to New York for graduate school at Columbia. “They didn’t think that landscape history, which is what I wanted to study, was academic enough. And they probably had no one to teach it anyway,” she claims. So she earned an MA and an MPhil in art history. Travel became a form of individualized study. “I learned by looking,” she says. She sought out Le Corbusier’s buildings in France, including La Tourette, Maisons Jaoul, and Villa Savoye, and drove from Paris to Santiago de Compostela looking at Romanesque and Merovingian churches. She made her first of many pilgrimages to Sissinghurst, a garden in Kent created by the writer Vita Sackville-West and her diplomat husband, Harold Nicolson. “There’s nothing more beautiful than Sissinghurst,” she sighs.

One of Nevins’s greatest champions has been Geffen, whom Victoria Newhouse, the renowned architecture critic and widow of longtime Condé Nast chairman Si Newhouse, introduced her to. On her first meeting with Geffen, Nevins arrived to present her work with a carousel of 80 slides. “After maybe 30 slides, he says, ‘That’s enough. You’re hired.’ And I thought to myself, Who is this guy?” When she looked him up, she read that one of his attributes is spotting talent. “And that was that.”.

According to recent reports, at the Warner estate in Beverly Hills, she removed one swimming pool to open up the landscape, built a latest one with a new patio house where Warner had a putting green, and relocated several mature oak trees on the property. “David is not afraid of major moves,” she notes. (They preserved the fountains and terraces Warner had commissioned from Florence Yoch, who designed the grounds of Tara for Gone With the Wind, of course.) However, according to Nevins, when Warner’s daughter came to see what Geffen had done, she looked around and asked if they had changed anything. “ ‘What did we change? We changed everything!’ ” Nevins remembers Geffen saying. “The idea that we didn’t do a thing is crazy, but that it looked like it was meant to be—that’s a good thing. The ultimate compliment that looks like I did nothing.”.

An aerial view of Deborah Nevins’s Hamptons garden.

In a recent development, hilfiger hired Nevins for a property in Mustique in the early 1990s, and again for his Denbigh Farm in Greenwich in 1995. In the Caribbean, she created palm promenades and a courtyard of white flowers; in Connecticut, she brought the elements of an old estate into a coherent whole. “I knew she was incredibly passionate about her work, and that always interested me because I love working with people who are passionate about what they do,” Hilfiger says. “Her execution was impeccable, and she delivered exactly what she promised.”.

Sources indicate that nevins’s office is based in Upcoming York City, and she keeps between 5 and 10 new projects going at all times. “Almost any job is interesting unless I hear in advance that the people aren’t nice,” she says. “Also, art collectors, in my experience, have been great patrons. If you’re an art collector—and you’re truly not collecting just to make money from art—you have an interest in beauty and understanding.”.

It has been revealed that PLEACHY KEEN “She is very intuitive, so she needs to walk a site and feel what it has to say,” architect Gil Schafer indicates of Nevins. “She feels this deep kinship with the natural world, with plants and with the trees of a site, which guides how she approaches her interventions on a property.”.

On average, it takes two years to get a garden up and running, three years if she needs to build new structures. But a garden is never finished. Roberta Denning, who with her husband, Steve, commissioned Nevins for her family’s property in Greenwich in 2006, describes the pleasure of living with something that acquires depth while continuing to change. “What she created has grown more valuable with time,” Denning says of her property, which includes a walking labyrinth among chestnuts and beech trees. “Nearly 20 years on, the gardens feel both that they have always been here and that they are continually renewed.” Nevins says clients have joked that hiring her is like a marriage because it’s a long-term relationship, and it requires work. “So I guess I’m a polygamist?” she smiles.

Patience is a major part of her process. “She is very intuitive, so she needs to walk a site and feel what it has to say, and this is one way that we are so similar in our approach,” Schafer says. “You need to give her the space to read the land and sort out how she wants to approach it. I think she also feels this deep kinship with the natural world, with plants and with the trees of a site, which guides how she approaches her interventions on a property.”.

Industry observers note that people joke that Nevins speaks to the plants, but Schafer isn’t sure it’s an act. “I think she really does!”.

“I do love them,” Nevins states of her botanical family. “I was at a nursery with someone the other day, and I stated, ‘It’s problematic. I get crushes on plants, but sometimes they don’t really have a place, and it’s so disappointing. It’s like a failed romance.’”.

A walking labyrinth in Greenwich, Connecticut.

Recent findings suggest that currently her crush is Stewartia pseudocamellia. “It has amazing bark, and the flower looks like a camellia, but it’s not a camellia, it’s a tree.” One plant she doesn’t love? Flowering forsythia, which Schafer reports she often refers to as “spring vomit.”.

Industry observers note that nevins believes her greatest asset is the ability to blend both architectural history and botanical skill. “I have such a strong academic background in architectural history,” she indicates. “I know exactly what these references are that they make to historical, even modern historical buildings.”.

Industry observers note that in another part of Long Island, Nevins combined the elements into what she calls a “beech house”—pun absolutely intentional. Martin Filler, an architecture critic and longtime contributor to The Upcoming York Review of Books, met Nevins when they were graduate students in Columbia’s art history department in the early 1970s. At the time, his wife, Rosemarie Haag Bletter, an architectural historian and professor emerita of art history at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York City, was working on her PhD and teaching undergraduates. According to Filler, Nevins promised back then to design them a garden one day. “Since we didn’t have a house and never expected to, we said to ourselves, ‘Yeah, right,’ ” he indicates. “But who knew that someday we would, and that gardening would become such a large part of our lives, especially Rosemarie’s?”.

In the mid-1990s, they bought a cottage that had been part of Stanford White’s Breese estate, The Orchard, in Southampton. “Debby stated that she would now make good on her promise to design a garden for us,” Filler remembers. “By that time she had become one of the top landscape designers, but she insisted on doing it and refused to be paid.” She stayed with them for a winter weekend and spent hours walking the property. “Then she sat down at our dining table with a roll of yellow tracing paper and the surveyor’s map, and she designed the whole thing within a few hours. She joked, ‘Don’t tell anyone how fast I was.’ ”.

According to recent reports, THE GIVING TREE When Derek C. Blasberg first saw the majestic tree in the backyard of a property in the Hamptons, he knew he’d found a home for his family. The hunt to identify it led him to Nevins’s larger body of work. “We could picture our children climbing its winding branches.”.

The Beech House, a 16-foot-by-16-foot-by-16-foot living gazebo made of 26 purple beech trees (Fagus sylvatica “Dawyck Purple”), is the centerpiece. The trees were sourced from Buffalo, trucked to Southampton, and replanted in the same orientation in which they had been grown. (“Each tree had to be marked with a dot of blue paint to indicate due north and then planted in that same geographical direction,” Filler remembers.) They were wired and trained over a wooden inner framework shaped like the schematic outline of a house and then clipped into shape on the exterior. The floor was paved with bluestone squares and rectangles in a random-looking pattern Nevins designed.

In a recent development, “Each year when we meet with our accountant to do our tax return, he’s always shocked that we spend so much on the garden,” Filler says. “We tell him: ‘You have clients who have boats, you have clients who have classic cars—well, this is our pleasure, our indulgence.’”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott remarked Call of Duty HQ's daily active owners (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 introduced on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a big bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to latest estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.

Sources indicate that writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott remarked Call of Duty HQ's daily active owners (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 introduced on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. On PlayStation, which Elliott describes as "CoD's main platform", the drop was 44 percent.

"Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote. "It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

It has been revealed that fortnite and FC 27 took a hit too, but both are already recovering. Fortnite's DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox fell 28 percent, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million, but by the end of the weekend it had clawed its way back to 19 percent below its baseline.

Epic is also holding a live event to close out the current season on 5th December, which Elliott indicates the studio "hopes will pull players back after they’ve polished off GTA 6’s story".

FC 27's DAUs dropped by around 27 percent, from 5.9 million to 4.3 million, and it's already back within 20 percent of its baseline.

Industry observers note that GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD (@alineaanalytics estimates).COD HQ's daily active customers across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M. On PlayStation – CoD’s main platform – Call of Duty took a 44% hit. Sadly, CoD has barely bounced… pic.twitter.com/XLa6N9TBfr.

According to Alinea, of those who'd played GTA 6 by the end of its launch weekend, 29 percent had also played Fortnite this month, 16 percent had played Call of Duty HQ, and 11 percent had played FC 27.

Elliott mentioned the pattern is largely what Alinea had predicted: the big live service games took an instant hit from GTA, but bounced back "because they're ingrained habits". Call of Duty is "the outlier here", he added, "and Xbox should - candidly - be worried about one of its premier franchises".

Elliott also points out that all of this is the impact of GTA 6's single-player mode. He expects its online component and PC port to arrive "some time next year", and when they do, he claims, "the bounce back will not be so obtainable".

Alinea also estimates that GTA 6 has sold 44.9 million copies and made more than $4 billion since launch.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. While it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

According to recent reports, eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Upcoming Jersey man was arrested after he allegedly fatally attacked his neighbor with a sword.

Middlesex County Prosecutor Linda Estremera and Chief James Ryan of the South Brunswick Police Department declared in a Saturday, November 21, news release that Jordan Williams has been charged with first-degree murder for his involvement in Altaray “Al” Cunningham’s death on Friday, November 20.

Williams, 28, was also charged with third-degree possession of a weapon for an unlawful purpose and fourth-degree unlawful possession of a weapon.

Authorities learned of the incident when the South Brunswick Police Department received a 911 call on Friday around 7:30 p.m. regarding a physical altercation that was taking place at the Royal Oaks Apartment Complex. Williams allegedly told Cunningham, 44, that he “had something” for him before he went into his apartment and returned with a large object, which witnesses said they believed was a type of stick, according to an affidavit viewed by NJ.com.

When officers reported to the scene, they found Cunningham suffering from blunt force trauma. He was ultimately pronounced dead at the scene.

Cunningham’s fiancée, Erin Bailey, claimed to ABC 7 that the attack was “premeditated.”.

“He took his last breaths with me,” Bailey stated, adding that “he couldn’t talk” in his final moments. “His face was just messed up. His face was distorted. It was so damaged and bloody.”.

Authorities identified Williams as the suspect, but he fled the scene before he could be taken into custody.

Recent findings suggest that “I was there when he came and tried to attack both of us. And my fiancé ran. And when he ran, he ran after him and attacked him,” Bailey said. “This was not ‘he went off and went crazy.’ No, he was waiting to act and kill.”.

Recent findings suggest that officers eventually found Williams in Woodbridge, Upcoming Jersey, around 2 a.m. on Saturday. Williams allegedly “refused to step out [of his car] and began to fumble around inside and continued to ignore our orders,” per the affidavit.

Williams then fled to Franklin Township, where Woodbridge police officers managed to catch up to him.

The defendant barricaded himself inside his vehicle, and he was eventually taken into custody after the Somerset County SWAT team deployed gas to remove him from the car. As one Somerset County SWAT officer tried to remove Williams, his gas mask was struck with the suspect’s sword.

Sources indicate that it’s not currently clear if Williams has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The South Brunswick Police Department did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment regarding updates in the case.

Following the tragedy, Bailey remarked she will remember Cunningham as “amazing fiancé,” who was “an amazing father [and] an amazing son.”.

Recent findings suggest that “He touched so many lives, and he served his community,” she said of Cunningham, whom she was in a relationship with for 10 years. “He didn’t deserve this at all.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another awards ceremony is struggling with how to handle an influx of genAI games. The Atari Homebrew Awards is in its ninth year, or at least it was going to be. It’s been canceled after its organizer hit an impasse with how to handle submissions that might have been made with AI.

According to recent reports, “Keeping up with the large number of AI assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI,” ZeroPage Homebrew wrote on the Atari Age forum (via Time Extension). “This flood of fresh AI games forced me reevaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.”.

The task for ZeroPage wasn’t simply going through all of the submissions; it was figuring out what cutoff, if any, to have for AI use. Allowing games that were 100-percent generated by AI was out of the question, but what about games that used AI for music, art, or coding? How much of the game could be made by AI before it went against the purpose of the whole awards ceremony?

Linked below an key announcement you should probably read. Please keep in mind this won't change the ZPH stream and we will keep playing all the awesome games made by the community!https://t.co/0odTADzfh9.

— ZeroPage Homebrew (@zeropagehomebre) November 23, 2026.

On top of that, there are no easy ways to vet the amount of AI used to make games. It requires that people honestly disclose it, leading to a grey area in which community reactions can lead to witch hunts and testing software can lead to false positives.

It has been revealed that “We were always able to come up with a solution for small issues in previous years but the advent of AI marked a seismic shift in the way retro games were being made,” ZeroPage wrote. “I saw no path forward and made the difficult decision to suspend the Atari Homebrew Awards this year.”.

The forum post now has hundreds of comments as consumers react to the news and debate AI’s place in the Atari homebrew scene and beyond. “Most people who use AI are tools. (derogatory),” one person wrote. Another remarked a “tool” was exactly what AI turned a work colleague of theirs into. “[He] told us how when he woke up in the middle of the night to go to the bathroom he would check if there was any pending question so he could unblock the AI agent,” the person wrote. “He also confessed he started to dread looking at his phone because answering would take 15-20 mins…his sleep patterns were going the way of the dodo.”.

Latest Update: Fan-favorite Diablo 2 anniversary bosses and items won't disappear when Diablo 4's next season starts

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season.
  • Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.
  • According to recent reports, on December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season. Blizzard shoved just about every iconic Diablo 2 boss and item it could think of into the modern game, and, by all accounts, it was one of the best seasons it ever had.

Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.

According to recent reports, on December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm. However, the craftable items, like the Enigma chest piece that gives you a free teleport skill, will not carry over.

In a recent development, even without all the craftable unique items, that's quite a lot of stuff to keep around. Blizzard tends to ditch seasonal additions as soon as a fresh season starts, and you usually have to wait a while to see them slipped back into the game in a slightly altered form. The overwhelming excitement around the Diablo 2 content must've convinced Blizzard it was worth putting in the work to keep them around.

Sources indicate that I would've been happy if the portal to Tristram, the rickety old town at the center of Diablo 2, was all that came back. Blizzard pulled off an incredibly faithful remake of it, complete with the old guitar theme and the voice of the blacksmith Griswold. And if you follow the hidden steps to make the Hellfire Torch, you'll be able to visit Uber Tristram, a special version of the town where you can square off against all three of the series' major villains, the Prime Evils, at once.

Diablo 4 was always kind of light on hidden quests and bosses, so it's nice to see that Blizzard found a way to bring an important part of the series back. I'll be curious to see what else comes to the game over the next three years before Diablo 5 arrives. The Amazon class will drop next year, but no expansions are planned to fill the gap. Hopefully Blizzard will take this opportunity to experiment with more things like the Diablo 2 anniversary secrets before it moves onto the sequel.

Industry observers note that I shared a straightforward childhood memory with a reporter about school and what was affordable for different families at the time. It wasn't intended as an attack on anyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has mentioned people can expect a similar qualitative and technological leap from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 as has been witnessed between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6.

CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski made the remark during a Q3 earnings call this afternoon, during which he and CDPR faced a handful of questions related to GTA 6.

"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," Nowakowski began by saying, "but I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game, we did see the differences.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 - I think so, yes. It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.".

Another question was about whether GTA 6 had affected development looks for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 - a question well-timed after Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski joked at the weekend that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled" because of how impressive GTA 6 is.

"Is seeing GTA 6 launch making us make the games more expensive?" noted Nowakowski. "We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's [that it's] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.".

Specifically in terms of budget, Nowakowski mentioned nothing had changed, and also echoed a point made earlier this year when he said Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 are "not budget-driven developments".

"I'm not saying we don't care about the budgets: we do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind 'this is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that's it, otherwise I'm gone'," he said.

It has been revealed that "They're ambition-driven developments and money's important - the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is like I stated, and honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release; it has just always been like that.".

Recent findings suggest that when asked whether the arrival of GTA 6 had impacted sales of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, Nowakowski answered "yes and no". "You do see a certain dip in engagement on the PlayStation and Xbox for sure," he said.

Sources indicate that statistics apparently show a drop of "at least" 25 percent in CDPR's players as they "engaged themselves with GTA 6". "But you do have to remember that a lot of our players are PC-based," Nowakowski pointed out. "GTA has not introduced on PC; we have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales or engagement. So it's a bit of a mixed answer.

Industry observers note that "And also on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero," he added. "Some short impact, yes, on the consoles. Long-term, we do not really see that affecting ourselves in any material way in Q4.".

Recent findings suggest that finally, the questioning turned to marketing, which Rockstar has shown can reach far and wide if you have the brand-power of GTA and some imagination. We've seen prestigious department stores like Selfridges taken over by Rockstar for GTA 6, trailers premiering on Netflix, Miami launch festivals - Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

CDPR is no stranger to grabbing headlines with glitzy actor hirings such as Keanu Reeves, but will Rockstar's approach to marketing GTA 6 push it a step further?

According to recent reports, "The most crucial takeaway - I'm not sure if I'd call it a lesson because this is our playbook as well - is that if you want to reach a certain critical mass, you do have to get out of just the core gaming bubble, something we did in the past as well," Nowakowski said. "For sure, GTA 6 went there.

Industry observers note that "If the underlying question was if we're going to repeat or copy-paste their playbook: no, for sure not. Our games are different and they require a certain different approach - we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: this is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future.".

CDPR's Q3 financial results were positive. The company made less money than this time last year, but the "fresh momentum" - as Nowakowski put it - provided to The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 by the release of the Remastered edition of Witcher 3 and the Edgerunners anime series on Netflix, and associated game upgrade, went a long way.

The Witcher 3 reached its highest concurrent player count on Steam as a result, and Cyberpunk 2077 reached its second highest concurrent player count, which represents serious staying power for both games so long after they were first released. And with Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past on track for 2027, and The Witcher 4 for 2028, the future is loaded.

It has been revealed that walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov in the original Star Trek series and seven Star Trek feature films, died on October 25 in Los Angeles, his rep confirmed. “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. He passed of old age at home in North Hollywood last night surrounded by his daughter and niece,” his rep mentioned in a statement. The statement continued, “Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond ‘Star Trek,’ his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft. His remarkable talent continued to shine in his later years, most recently with his performance in the short film ‘Mr. Fleischmann,’ for which he received the Platinum Award for Best Actor at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards — a fitting recognition of a lifetime devoted to his craft.” The statement also noted Koenig’s “kindness, wit and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him.” “He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it,” the statement concluded. “On behalf of all of us, we extend our deepest condolences to Walter’s family, friends, colleagues, and the millions of fans whose lives he touched over the decades. Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before.”.

RJ Mitte, known for playing Walter “Flynn” White Jr. on AMC’s Breaking Bad, died at age 34 on October 12. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” his rep said in a statement to Us. Recalling his time on Breaking Bad, the statement continued, “Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion.” (Mitte was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at age 3.) “Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s,” his rep added. “He also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, supporting philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, while using his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities.” The statement concluded, “At this time, we ask people to respect the privacy of RJ Mitte’s family and close ones.".

Saved by the Bell star Dennis Haskins’ rep revealed to Us on September 28 that the Mr. Belding actor had died at age 75. No cause of death was immediately disclosed. “It’s a tragic loss,” his spokesperson told Us. “Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis, loved him even more.” The statement concluded, “[Dennis] was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans. He always had time for them, no matter what. He was my client and dear friend for over 20 years, and I will miss him terribly. Industry observers note that the longtime NHL coach and ESPN analyst’s death at age 70 was revealed on September 9. Melrose retired as one of ESPN’s color commentators in October 2023 after being diagnosed with Parkinson’s Disease. “From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman stated in a statement. "You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey." ESPN also paid tribute via a statement, which read, “For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey. His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing, and his passion was unmistakable. He was a foundational part of ESPN's hockey coverage, and fans and teammates truly appreciated his entertaining delivery and charismatic personality. "We send our deepest condolences to his loved ones. He always kept it interesting and he will be missed,” a network spokesperson added.

According to recent reports, “Jolene” singer and country legend Dolly Parton died at age 80 on August 25, her rep confirmed in a statement. “Global icon and humanitarian, Dolly Parton, known to the world as a beloved singer, songwriter, philanthropist, actress, playwright, and author died peacefully today in Nashville, Tennessee,” the statement read. “A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family.” Her rep continued: “Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact.” Per Parton’s request, a “small, private service will be held for immediate family,” and her “fans and friends from around the world are encouraged to pay tribute to Dolly on social media and her website.” The statement concluded, “In lieu of flower, the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library.".

The Challenge alum Tyler Duckworth’s mother, Joni, announced on August 13 that her son had died at age 44 earlier in the week. No cause of death has been determined as of publication. Duckworth was a pioneer for LGBTQ+ contestants on The Challenge as a two-time winner of the Cutthroat and Rivals seasons. Many Challenge cast members paid tribute to the late reality star following the announcement of his death. “Absolutely heartbroken to hear about Tyler. We shared something special being part of The Challenge family,” Brad Fiorenza wrote via Instagram. “I’ll always be grateful for the memories we shared; especially at this last event just a couple weeks ago. Tyler will be deeply missed by so many. May his amazing soul live on in the lives he’s touched. RIP my dear friend 🕊️🙏” The Challenge star Tina Barta shared her own memorial message, writing, “Some friendships are measured in years. Others are measured in memories, laughter, shared experiences and the way someone makes you feel when they are in the room. @themightyduckworth you are one of those special people. A true friend and confidant.💔… Tyler, thank you for being part of my story. I’m grateful our paths crossed in this crazy life and that I get to carry those memories with me. Rest peacefully, my darling friend 🕊️.”.

Reggie Bannister died at age 80 on August 9 at his cabin in Crestline, California, his wife Gigi confirmed to TMZ. The South African Football Players Union announced Mamelodi Sundowns and Bafana Bafana midfielder Jayden Adams' death on July 11, only a few weeks after he competed in the World Cup. No cause of death was immediately announced. “His passing is an immeasurable loss to his family, teammates, clubs, the football fraternity and the country at large,” the organization stated in a statement. “Death has cruelly stolen one of our own. It has robbed our nation of a remarkable footballer, but it will never take away the legacy Jayden Adams leaves behind. We will forever remember his humanity, his extraordinary talent and the pride with which he represented South Africa.” “There are no words to describe the pain I’m feeling. 💔 “Rest in peace, my love,” Adams’ girlfriend Aqueelah Chloe Adendorf wrote via Instagram. “Thank you for every memory, every laugh, every hug, and every moment we shared. You were not only the love of my life but also my greatest supporter and my best friend." She went on, “A part of my heart left with you, and I will carry your love with me forever. Until we meet again, I’ll miss you every single day. Rest easy, my angel. I love you always and forever." FIFA president Gianni Infantino added in his own statement, “It is so incredibly sad to hear that South Africa midfielder Jayden Adams has passed away just weeks after featuring in his nation’s historic FIFA World Cup campaign. My thoughts and condolences, as well as those of everyone at FIFA and the global football community, are with his family, friends and teammates. The Bafana and Mamelodi Sundowns star will be sorely missed. May he rest in peace.”.

  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida. If you take a detour along the north side of Lummox County, you'll come across an area in the woods that looks like it'd be right at home in a Super Mario Bros. game, and you can even collect two distinct caps for your troubles--which might suggest that the greater Mario multiverse theory is true after all. How to find the GTA 6 Super Mario Bros. Easter egg in GTA 6 You can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County. It's up north from Mount Kalaga, at the end of a twisty road that seemingly goes nowhere: Hit the bong, dude Once you've arrived, scout the area for a purple tarp that has a bong sitting on it. Smoke it, get high, and climb the structure in front of you. You'll notice that there's a plume of smoke coming out of the one column, and if you stand in it, an invisible block will appear above your head. Smash the block Jump up, and you'll smash the block. You won't get any gold coins for your trouble, but you will get a nostalgic tune and two caps that reference Nintendo's favorite plumbers, Mario and Luigi. Collect the caps Each cap has an initial embroidered on it: "J" for Jason, "L" for Lucia. You can add them to your collection, or leave them to gather dust; it's up to you. As mentioned above, GTA 6 has references to a lot of pop culture. Someone at Rockstar Games is clearly a huge Dexter fan, Bigfoot is on the prowl, and I really wish I'd chosen the elevator without a killer clown inside it. For everything else on the biggest game of the year--and maybe even the decade--check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub.

#188818. From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1567 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple.
  • November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.
  • Sources indicate that the Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.

Sources indicate that the Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was noted to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

The couple on their engagement, 1947.

It has been revealed that in 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately remarked yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day.

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

Recent findings suggest that like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

In a recent development, designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

It has been revealed that princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

As Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”.

Princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, mentioned to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

Industry observers note that all royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

Sources indicate that the wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages.

There were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

Together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.).

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”.

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

On the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace.

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

Although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake.

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

Over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards are now open, and to mark the event's 10th anniversary, Valve has brought back some categories from years past and added a Hall of Fame.

According to recent reports, you've got until 6pm UK (10am Pacific) on 30th November to nominate your favourite games of the year across 14 categories. Returning throwbacks include Just 5 More Minutes, Defies Description, and This is My Job Now, which recognises games that simulate mundane real-life jobs.

The new Hall of Fame category will appear when voting opens, and will let players choose their favourite from Steam's previous Game of the Year winners to crown the best game of the past decade.

Most categories are only open to games released on Steam since last year's Autumn Sale.

The exception is the Labo(u)r of Love award, which goes to older games that developers are still supporting with upcoming content. Previous Labo(u)r of Love winners, including Warframe, Grand Theft Auto 5, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3, can't be nominated again.

It has been revealed that five finalists will be revealed in each category when voting opens alongside the Steam Winter Sale on 17th December. Voting closes at 10am Pacific on 2nd January, and the winners will be declared straight afterwards.

Nominating in at least one category also earns you the first level of Steam's Nomination Committee badge.

Earlier this month, Valve released a new Steam patch that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do.
  • According to recent reports, it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

Sources indicate that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

According to recent reports, it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive world filled with an incredible amount of detail and simulation. This includes the game’s dynamic and realistic weather system, a feature Rockstar hyped up quite a bit before launch. However, some players online aren’t seeing much rain and are claiming Rockstar lied. The reality is that, yes, rainstorms happen, but you might not be seeing them very often for a few reasons.

If you search around Reddit or Twitter, you’ll see a lot of people complaining that it never rainsÂ in GTA 6. However, you can also find amazing clips of thunderstorms pummeling Vice City. And I can confirm that when I played GTA 6 pre-release, I saw rainstorms and other weather events, like fog.Â  So what’s going on here? Why are some people suggesting the weather system in GTA 6 isn’t working or was a lie, while others, like myself, are dealing with thunderstorms?

It has been revealed that THIS ISN'T JUST RAIN. THIS IS ENVIRONMENTAL ARTISTRY AT AN ABSURD LEVEL! ð¤¯.

Just look at the rain dripping off the sides of the bridge, the incredibly atmospheric overcast skies and the way the entire scene comes together. GTA 6 genuinely looks like a work of art!

I'm quiteâ¦ pic.twitter.com/NjbjmeYHV7.

— VideoGameDetails (@VideoGameDetail) November 24, 2026.

First up is that it does seem like something was borked with GTA 6‘s dynamic weather system at launch. On Monday, the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 arrived and fixed an concern that, according to Rockstar’s patch notes, led to the weather not changing for extended periods of time. So yeah, one reason it might not have been raining in your game is because of a bug.

Recent findings suggest that however, even after the patch, some people are still claiming it isn’t raining in GTA 6. And maybe something is still bugged. The more likely explanation is that people don’t realize just how dynamic and advanced the weather is in GTA 6.

In all previous Grand Theft Auto games and most other open-world games, when it rains in the game, it rains across the whole map. That’s not how weather in GTA 6 works. Instead, storms, fog, and other weather events can happen locally and in small parts of the map. At one point I was flying a plane and it was sunny, but ahead in the sky were big dark clouds. As I reached them, I entered a rainstorm. As I left the clouds behind, the rain stopped. So it’s very possible that it is raining somewhere in your GTA 6 world; you just aren’t in the spot where the rain is falling.

It has been revealed that I’ve also seen some people suggesting the weather is locked to certain conditions earlier in the game, which seems plausible but hasn’t been confirmed by Rockstar yet. Once I reached chapter three of the game, I had a few in-game days when it rained a lot. I started to miss the sun.

Industry observers note that the point is that, no, Rockstar didn’t lie. Grand Theft Auto 6‘s dynamic weather system is so good that I think some people are just dodging the rain without realizing it. The size of the map and the randomness at play in the system may mean that you go for a while without encountering rainy weather, but keep playing and sooner or later, the storms will come.

It's also set a new record for concurrent players on the PS5.

The race to port GTA 6 to PC, explained

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (862 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, things are moving fast.
  • According to recent reports, what we do know for sure is that Rockstar is taking notice and has already begun cracking down on the highest-profile projects.
  • For now, the only thing to do is observe and report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, things are moving fast. Now that an illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 is out in the wild, anonymous modders are racing to port it to PC, and the work is progressing faster than many expected. At this rate, it's possible that a static recompilation of GTA 6 will run on a PC in a matter of days. It's also possible it will take much longer to produce a playable build that's actually on par with the console versions.

According to recent reports, what we do know for sure is that Rockstar is taking notice and has already begun cracking down on the highest-profile projects. As always, downloading pirated software is illegal and can infect your PC with malware, and that last bit is doubly true in the dubious AI era we now live in.

For now, the only thing to do is observe and report. Here's where things stand with GTA 6 PC ports.

Several projects have made it as far as booting the game and using menus, and at least one has seemingly managed to move around in-game with bugged out lighting, but it's hard to verify clips making the rounds when so many are obvious fakes.

Dozens of groups of anonymous modders and vibecoders. So many, in fact, that several websites dedicated to tracking the progress of GTA 6 recomp efforts have also appeared. One of the tracker sites, Portwatch VI, has a list of projects ranked by their "playable" completion percentage—best not to take those made up figures as an accurate estimate of when a port will be complete. The top five are:.

Until very recently, the Leonida project was among those making impressive progress, but the group's creator (a 15-year-old) quit the project after Rockstar got its Discord server taken down.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Every GTA 6 recomp project is based on the same thing: An illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 released online by Cyberleek, the notorious leaker who previously shared video of a GTA 6 development build months before its release.

With GTA 6 being the biggest game in the world at the moment and not available on PC, there is an outsized motivation to get it running.

A recomp refers to static recompilation, which is the result of reverse-engineering a game's code to make it run on other hardware (usually a PC). If you want to read further on how that's achieved, PCG alum Wes Fenlon's excellent Read Only Memo newsletter has what you're looking for.

As for how GTA 6 ports (and ports for other upcoming games) are coming together so rapidly, the answer is AI. The advent of AI coding tools like Claude have greatly expedited the work required to create a static recompilation of games on another platform. What used to take months to years now takes hours to days. Recomps that heavily use AI are often buggier, messier, and have fewer features than human-made fan projects, but they are fast and functional.

It's way too early to speak in absolutes, but I'm comfortable assuming that the first "playable" recomps will require an exceptionally powerful PC.

That guess is based on GTA 6 being an obviously demanding game and also some recent precedent: The earliest Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake recomps that've appeared online have high system requirements to perform as well as it does natively on Switch 2—and, well, GTA 6 has a lot more happening under the hood than a 28-year-old Zelda game.

According to recent reports, that's the big question. My money is on no, it won't. To switch up looks on a dime would assume that Rockstar is sitting on a polished PC version that it could put out any day, and I'm not convinced that's the case. The current rumor, preceding all of this leak business, is that the PC version of GTA 6 is planned for Q1 2027 (so anytime before April).

That's not to say Rockstar couldn't expedite the process if it wanted to—they certainly have the resources to achieve the unlikely.

Morgan is a beat writer following the latest and greatest shooters and the communities that play them. He also writes general news, reviews, features, the occasional guide, and bad jokes in Slack. #188813. GTA 6: All The Secret Controls And Gameplay Features You Might Have Missed

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2886 w)

GTA 6: All The Secret Controls And Gameplay Features You Might Have Missed

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that on the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • On the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • Instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists. You've got everything you'd expect for exploring its open-world environment, from options to sprint to aiming your gun, but there's a whole lot more to the game when you start experimenting with the inputs. Whether you're driving or jogging, Jason and Lucia are capable of a whole lot more, and these hidden features aren't thrown at you when you start the game. Instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience. If you don't want to accidentally stumble on them, here's a closer look at every hidden gameplay feature we've discovered so far. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub. Go into first-person mode Want to examine the world in more detail around you? Press L2 (LT on Xbox) to highlight something, then press R3 to go into first-person mode. Ordinarily, you can't move around in this mode, but there is a glitch to force the game to lock you into first-person. Change shoulder cameras Not too significant a fan of the default over-the-shoulder aiming in GTA 6? You can switch which shoulder you aim from during combat by holding the left button on your D-pad while aiming with L2. Quick-swap between weapons At the same time, you can also quick-swap between weapons by tapping Triangle/Y while aiming, allowing you to keep blastin' like you're some sort of Frank Reynolds character. Do a combat roll! Need to close the gap quickly and avoid taking a few lead injections? Tap X/A while aiming, and you'll do a combat roll. Do a backflip! To show off some athleticism, run towards water, and as you get to the edge, hold X/A on the controller to do a backflip. Pistol-whip when you're out of bullets Got a gun in your hand, but you're out of bullets? It turns out that firearms are still good for inflicting blunt-force trauma, as you can use the melee attack (Square on PS5, X on Xbox) to knock enemies out. Choke enemies out For a stealthy beatdown, start a fight in GTA 6, grapple your opponent with R2, and then hold Square/X to set them up for a chokehold. Press the indicated D-pad button on your controller, and you'll trigger the chokehold. Chain-jump across gaps If you're running across an area that has multiple small gaps, you can tap X to jump across and tap it again to keep your momentum going. Your car door is also a weapon Instead of damaging the hood of your car in GTA 6, put a dent in your door by smashing it into a pedestrian. Like melee attacks, you can hit Square/X on your controller while driving to nail an unlucky person with the door. Your feet are technically free when you're on a bike And if you're not in a car? You can relive your Road Rash days by hitting the melee button to kick someone instead while you scoot around on a bike. Change how you wear your cap Whether you like to wear your cap in a traditional sun-blocking style or backwards, you can swap the position of your headwear easily. Just open the items and weapon wheel by holding L1, select items, and navigate to your cap. Press X/A and you can switch styles. Distract enemies with some whistling, which I can't do in real life GTA 6 makes for a surprisingly good stealth game, and for those scenarios where you need to draw enemy attention, you can whistle at them. Crouch, take cover, hold L2 to aim at a target, and press Triangle/Y to whistle. Loiter like a champ with leaning actions One of the cooler features in GTA 6 for photography fans is the option to lean against walls and railings. When you're near a wall, you can hold Circle/B to lean against it, and when next to a railing, press L3 to rest on that structure--pretty cool for when you want to take a photograph of Jason or Lucia while they chill out. If you're on solid ground, you can also hold down Circle/B to sit down. Choose your favorite hand If you want Jason or Lucia to emulate your dominant hand while they're holding something, press left or right on the D-pad. You can also make them hold two items at the same time, in case you want to show off that you're one of the lucky even-handed few. Auto-drive to destinations  One of our favorite modes in the game--especially when we want to soak in the scenery of Vice City--auto-drive is pretty easy to miss. While you're driving, hold the down button on the D-pad, press Start to enable Cinematic Mode, and then hold Circle/B to switch to auto-drive mode. You can also set the speed between slow/normal/fast for your commute. Quick-scan vehicles Instead of navigating to your WAiNK app, just hold Up on your D-Pad to bring it up instantly. Duck while driving so you can avoid being shot You're going to be in plenty of high-speed shootouts in GTA 6, and if you want to keep your head on your shoulders, hold the Circle/B button while driving to duck down. You have turn signals; use them Unless you're driving the equivalent of a BMW in GTA 6, you should use turn signals. While you're in your car, tap left or right on your D-pad to use these lights. They'll also cancel automatically after you've made a turn. Switch car headlights on and off Want to drive in stealth mode at night? Tap the circle button to turn off your headlights. Just don't be too surprised if other motorists flash you with their lights to remind you that you're driving dark. Leave the engine running Want to prepare your vehicle to be in getaway mode for a heist that you're about to pull off? You can leave the engine running by double-tapping Triangle/Y as you exit your car. Just be aware that this could invite car thieves to swipe your vehicle, since you're leaving it out there and purring. If you do this while piloting a boat, it'll also sail on while you explore the deck. Push vehicles In case you're stuck in a ditch or out of fuel, you can push your vehicle to safety. Position yourself behind, next to, or in front of your car (or boat), and keep pushing your character into it with the left stick until they switch to a pushing animation. Hold Square/X to move the vehicle, or flip it in case it has been overturned or beached. Leave your car door open You can also shave valuable seconds off your getaway by keeping your car door open. As you exit your car, press triangle once. Slide across your car hood For some Dukes of Hazzard action, sprint towards your car, aim for the hood, and tap X to slide across it. Yeehaw. Drop anchor If you don't want your boat to sail away without you while you search the ocean depths for treasure, make certain that you drop anchor. Press and hold left on the D-pad while piloting a boat, navigate to the vehicle menu with the right analog stick, and choose Anchor to lower it. Additional vehicle controls On that note, you can also find extra vehicle controls by bringing up the radio menu (press and hold left on the D-pad), and using the right analogue stick to navigate up. Turn radios on and off instantly If you're anything like me and your ears start to bleed when you boost a car that has the country music station turned on, double-tap left on the D-pad to instantly switch it off. You can smoke while driving Not that you should because it's bad for your health and both hands should be on the steering wheel, but you can hold L1 to bring up your items wheel, select cigarettes or a cigar, and then select R1 or R2 to start puffing away. Flick a cigarette You can also flick your cigarette when you're done smoking by holding the R2 button. Aim, and do that after you've poured out a trail of fuel on the ground, for extra cinema-style points. Flip the bird while driving The universal hand sign for telling someone that their driving is not up to par can easily be done by aiming at a motorist with L2 and then pressing R1 on your controller. Trash talk drivers Or if you need to give some verbal abuse, pull up next to another driver, press L2 to aim at them, and press R3 to give them some grief. Just don't be too surprised if they respond violently to your provocations.

Who Will Be The Next Bond Girl?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair
